q-82194.name: Question 1
q-82194.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 3\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0.5 \\ 3 & -3 & \sqrt{5} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}|
$$
q-82194.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The matrix $A$ has identical columns: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|A|=0.$

- The matrix $B$ has a zero row: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0.5 \\ 3 & -3 & \sqrt{5} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- Since $C$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain 

$$
|C|=7\cdot (-1)\cdot (-2)=14\ne 0.
$$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|B|$ are equal to $0.$

Which of the following determinants are equal to 0?

|A|=|2−1021031−71−1−73033|,|B|=|0−20.53−35000|,|C|=|7100−1300−2|

a
|B| only
b
|B| and |C| only
c
|A| and |C| only
d
|A| and |B| only
e
|A| only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

  • The matrix A has identical columns: A=[2−1021031−71−1−73033] As a result, |A|=0.

  • The matrix B has a zero row: B=[0−20.53−35000] As a result, |B|=0.

  • Since C is a triangular matrix, we obtain |C|=7⋅(−1)⋅(−2)=14≠0.

Therefore, only |A| and |B| are equal to 0.

q-82192.name: Question 2
q-82192.worked_solution:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

- Since $A$ has two identical columns, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,det(A)=0.
$$

- Since $B$ is a triangular matrix, its determinant is given by the product of the elements of the main diagonal: 

$$
det(B)=3\cdot (-1)\cdot 1\cdot 2=-6
$$

Therefore, $7det(A)-2det(B)=7\cdot 0-2\cdot (-6)=12.$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{5} & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}4 & \sqrt{3} & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}|

$$

- Since $B$ is a diagonal matrix, we obtain 

$$

$$

As a result, $|C|=0.$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

q-82193.name: Question 4
q-82193.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & \sqrt{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$
q-82193.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- Since $A$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain 

$$
|A|=5\cdot (-1)\cdot 2=-10\ne 0.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has a zero column: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- The matrix $C$ has identical rows: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

q-140046.problem:

$$

$$

$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- Since $C$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix, its determinant is:

$$
det(C)=5\cdot 4-(-2)\cdot (-10)=0
$$

Therefore, only $|B|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$
